A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N‐substituent of the peptide PXXP‐motif is able to improve the peptide binding affinity to the target domain by establishing additional interactions.

the systematic N‐amidation of peptide PXXPP sequence is a promising strategy for the design of SH3‐binding peptides with high affinity, which could be extended to the development of peptide therapeutics targeting the SH3 domains.
the peptide PXXP‐motif can be modified by N‐substitution with the nonnatural amino acids, which can be applied in the molecular design of peptide inhibitors and drug candidates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peptide affinity to the PLCγ SH3 domain can be enhanced by N‐substituting two key proline amino acids in SLP76‐based PXXP motif.

the N‐substituents are a promising class of amino acid replacements for the design of peptides with enhanced affinity to the PLCγ SH3 domain, which may have potential therapeutic value for the development of T‐cell immunotherapy.
N‐substituents can be introduced to the peptide backbone to enhance the peptide activity and the N‐substitution is not limited to proline.
